title: Ablating Persistent Structured State Collapses a Weak-Model Scaffolding Harness: A Seed-Matched Component Study
description:
A seed-matched component-ablation study testing which part of a scaffolding harness lets a weak 4-billion-parameter language model (gemma3:4b) succeed on a 200-day business-operations simulator with Vending-Bench economics.

Across N=100 matched seeds, a naive one-call-per-day model baseline fails 100% of runs (median net worth $83), a deterministic scripted policy 59% ($29), and the full harness 46% ($1,415). A component ablation is strongly asymmetric: removing persistent structured state collapses performance to 100% failure and a median net worth below the naive baseline, while removing the rarely-binding financial gates does not measurably change median performance or the failure rate. A seat-level ablation identifies model-mediated pricing as a necessary contributor to the full harness's advantage over the scripted policy.

This record includes the paper, the Kotlin/JVM harness, and dependency-free reproducibility scripts. The raw run databases (679 SQLite files) are distributed as a GitHub release asset. Code and data: https://github.com/bigshotClay/SuperVend9000
